lessons.title: Ratios in similar right triangles
objectives: You will be able to identify corresponding sides of similar right-angled triangles.
You will be able to calculate side ratios in similar triangles and see that they stay the same for the same angle.
You will be able to explain why trigonometric ratios depend on the angle, not on the size of the triangle.

keyWords.meaning: A triangle with one angle equal to 90 degrees.
The side opposite the right angle; always the longest side.
Triangles with the same angles; written ABC ||| DEF, with sides in the same ratio.
Sides that match up in the same position in two similar triangles.
One length divided by another length, written as a fraction.
A fixed ratio of two sides of a right-angled triangle that depends only on the angle.

blocks.text:
Trigonometry studies how the angles and the sides of a triangle are connected. In this lesson we start with similar right-angled triangles and the ratios of their sides.

Here is the big idea: if two right-angled triangles have the same angles, their sides grow by the same factor, so every ratio of two sides is the same in both triangles. This is what makes trigonometry work.
blocks.speech: Trigonometry studies how the angles and sides of a triangle are connected. We start with similar right-angled triangles. If two right-angled triangles have the same angles, their sides grow by the same factor, so every ratio of two sides is the same in both triangles. That one idea is the foundation of all of trigonometry.

blocks.caption: A 30-60-90 triangle: the hypotenuse AC is 2, the side opposite 30° is 1.
blocks.speech: The picture shows a right-angled triangle A B C. The right angle is at B. The angle at A is thirty degrees and the angle at C is sixty degrees. The side A C, opposite the right angle, is the hypotenuse and has length two. The side B C, opposite the thirty degree angle, has length one. The side A B has length root three.

blocks.text:
When triangle ABC ||| triangle DEF, the letters are written in matching order: A matches D, B matches E, C matches F. Then the angles match (A = D, B = E, C = F) and the ratios of corresponding sides are equal:

AB/DE = BC/EF = AC/DF

It also means AB/BC = DE/EF, and so on. Getting the order of the letters right is the first skill of this topic.
blocks.speech: When triangle A B C is similar to triangle D E F, the letters are written in matching order. A matches D, B matches E, and C matches F. The angles match, and the ratios of corresponding sides are equal. A B over D E equals B C over E F equals A C over D F. Getting the order of the letters right matters: triangle A B C similar to triangle D F E would be wrong.

blocks.problem: Triangle ABC has angle A = 30°, right angle at B and angle C = 60°, with AB = √3, BC = 1 and AC = 2. Calculate BC/AC, AB/AC and BC/AB.

steps.line: Right angle at B, so AC is the hypotenuse
steps.reason: The hypotenuse is always the side opposite the right angle
BC is opposite the 30° angle, AC is the hypotenuse
AB is the third side, divided by the hypotenuse
The side opposite 30° divided by the side next to it

blocks.speech: The problem: in triangle A B C, the angle at A is thirty degrees, the right angle is at B, and the sides are root three, one and two. First, the right angle is at B, so A C is the hypotenuse. B C over A C is one over two. A B over A C is root three over two. And B C over A B is one over root three.

blocks.problem: Triangle DEF ||| triangle ABC has the same angles (30°, 90°, 60°) but DE = 5√3, EF = 5 and DF = 10. Calculate EF/DF, DE/DF and EF/DE.

steps.line: Right angle at E, so DF is the hypotenuse
steps.reason: Same shape as ABC, scaled up by a factor of 5
Corresponding to BC/AC in the small triangle
Corresponding to AB/AC in the small triangle
Corresponding to BC/AB; every ratio is unchanged

blocks.speech: Now a bigger triangle, D E F, similar to A B C, with sides root three times five, five and ten. The right angle is at E, so D F is the hypotenuse. E F over D F is five over ten, which is one half. D E over D F is five root three over ten, which is root three over two. E F over D E is five over five root three, which is one over root three. Every ratio is exactly the same as in the small triangle.

blocks.text:
Look at what happened: the second triangle is 5 times bigger than the first, but the ratios BC/AC = 1/2 and 5/10 = 1/2 are identical.

This is the key fact of trigonometry: in a right-angled triangle, the ratio of any two sides depends only on the size of the angle, not on how big the triangle is. Any triangle with a 30° angle gives BC/AC = 1/2, always.
blocks.speech: Notice what happened. The second triangle is five times bigger, yet the ratios are identical: one half in both. This is the key fact of trigonometry. In a right-angled triangle, the ratio of any two sides depends only on the size of the angle, not on how big the triangle is. Every right-angled triangle with a thirty degree angle gives that ratio of one half.

blocks.problem: A 45-45-90 triangle PQR has PQ = 3, QR = 3 and PR = 3√2 (hypotenuse). A larger 45-45-90 triangle has legs 6 and 6, hypotenuse 6√2. Compare PQ/PR with the corresponding ratio in the large triangle.

steps.reason: Leg opposite the 45° angle over the hypotenuse; the 3s cancel
Same ratio, legs over hypotenuse; the 6s cancel
The ratio is the same for both sizes

blocks.speech: The problem: two 45, 45, 90 triangles, one with legs three and three, hypotenuse three root two, and one with legs six and six, hypotenuse six root two. In the small triangle, P Q over P R is three over three root two, which is one over root two. In the large one, six over six root two is also one over root two. Different sizes, same ratio, because the angles are the same.

blocks.problem: A ramp makes a 30° angle with the ground. A surveyor draws a small right-angled triangle of this ramp with hypotenuse 4, and measures the vertical rise as 2. A builder uses a scale model with hypotenuse 400. Without measuring, what is the vertical rise in the model?

steps.reason: Compute the ratio in the small triangle

steps.line: Angle is the same (30°), so the ratio is the same
steps.reason: Similar right-angled triangles have equal side ratios
Set up the equal ratio for the model
Multiply both sides by 400

blocks.speech: The problem: a ramp makes a thirty degree angle. A small drawn triangle has hypotenuse four and vertical rise two. A scale model has hypotenuse four hundred. What is the rise in the model? In the small triangle, rise over hypotenuse is two over four, one half. The angle is the same, so the ratio is the same. So rise over four hundred is one half, which gives a rise of two hundred.

question.prompt: A right-angled triangle XYZ has angle X = 45°, right angle at Y, XY = 4, YZ = 4 and XZ = 4√2. Calculate YZ/XZ (leave it in surd form).
steps: Right angle at Y, so XZ is the hypotenuse
question.why: Learners often divide the hypotenuse by the leg, or forget that the 4s cancel.
question.rightWay: XZ is opposite the right angle, so it is the hypotenuse. YZ/XZ = 4/(4√2) = 1/√2.

blocks.hint: First find the hypotenuse, then divide the side opposite 45° by it and cancel.
blocks.speech: Your turn. Triangle X Y Z has a right angle at Y, angle X is forty five degrees, and the sides are four, four and four root two. Calculate Y Z over X Z in surd form. Hint: find the hypotenuse first, then divide and cancel.

blocks.why: The order of the letters shows which vertex matches which. Writing DFE puts the angles in the wrong positions, so the corresponding sides are paired wrongly and every ratio is wrong.
blocks.speech: A common mistake: writing triangle A B C similar to triangle D F E, so that A B over D F equals B C over F E. The right way is triangle A B C similar to triangle D E F, so A B over D E equals B C over E F. The order of the letters tells you which vertex matches which. Wrong order means the sides are paired wrongly and the ratios come out wrong.

blocks.text:
Tying it together: similar right-angled triangles have equal angles, and equal angles force equal side ratios. So for a given angle like 30°, the ratio opposite/hypotenuse is one fixed number, whatever the size of the triangle.

A ratio of two sides that depends only on the angle is called a trigonometric ratio. In the next lesson we give these ratios their names: sine, cosine and tangent.
blocks.speech: To tie it together: similar right-angled triangles have equal angles, and equal angles force equal side ratios. So for a given angle like thirty degrees, the ratio of opposite over hypotenuse is one fixed number, whatever the size of the triangle. A ratio of two sides that depends only on the angle is called a trigonometric ratio. In the next lesson we name these ratios sine, cosine and tangent.

summary: Similar triangles ABC ||| DEF must be named in corresponding order: A matches D, B matches E, C matches F.
In similar triangles, ratios of corresponding sides are equal: AB/DE = BC/EF = AC/DF.
The hypotenuse is always opposite the right angle and never changes position.
For the same angle, every side ratio is the same no matter how big the triangle is.
This is why trigonometric ratios depend on the angle only, not on the size of the triangle.

practice.prompt: A right-angled triangle has a 30° angle, opposite side 3 and hypotenuse 6. Calculate opposite/hypotenuse.
practice.why: Learners sometimes write hypotenuse/opposite instead, giving 2.
practice.rightWay: Put the side opposite the angle on top and the hypotenuse underneath: 3/6 = 1/2.

practice.prompt: Triangle ABC ||| triangle DEF and AB/BC = 2/3. What is DE/EF?
steps: Corresponding sides of similar triangles have equal ratios
practice.why: Learners sometimes flip the ratio or use a different pair of sides.
practice.rightWay: Corresponding ratios in similar triangles are equal, so DE/EF = AB/BC = 2/3.

practice.prompt: A 45-45-90 triangle has legs 5 and 5 and hypotenuse 5√2. Calculate leg/hypotenuse in surd form.
practice.why: Learners forget the 5s cancel and try to work with 5√2 on the top.
practice.rightWay: 5/(5√2) = 1/√2. The same ratio holds in every 45-45-90 triangle.

practice.prompt: In triangle ABC ||| triangle DEF, AC/BC = 3/4. Which of these must also be true? A: DF/EF = 3/4, B: DF/EF = 4/3, C: AB/DE = 3/4
steps: A matches D, C matches F, so AC corresponds to DF and BC to EF
practice.why: Learners confuse which sides correspond, especially when the letters are in a different order.
practice.rightWay: Match the letters in order: A with D and C with F, so AC corresponds to DF and BC to EF, giving DF/EF = 3/4.

practice.prompt: Why does the ratio opposite/hypotenuse stay the same when a right-angled triangle is enlarged? A: Because the sides all get bigger, B: Because the angles stay the same and all sides scale by the same factor, C: Because the hypotenuse never changes
steps: All sides are multiplied by the same scale factor
So every ratio of two sides is unchanged
choices: Because the sides all get bigger
Because the angles stay the same and all sides scale by the same factor
practice.why: Learners often think bigger triangles change the ratios.
practice.rightWay: Enlarging multiplies every side by the same factor and keeps the angles, so all side ratios stay the same.

practice.prompt: A 30-60-90 triangle has hypotenuse 8. What is the length of the side opposite the 30° angle? (Hint: the ratio opposite/hypotenuse is 1/2 for every 30° angle.)
practice.why: Learners sometimes halve the wrong side or forget the ratio is fixed by the angle.
practice.rightWay: The ratio opposite/hypotenuse is 1/2 for any 30° angle, so the opposite side is 8 × 1/2 = 4.

practice.prompt: A ladder leans against a wall at 60° to the ground. In a scale drawing the ladder (hypotenuse) is 10 cm and the wall side is 5√3 cm. A real ladder is 6 m long. Calculate the height the real ladder reaches up the wall, in metres.
steps: Same angle (60°), so the ratio is the same: h/6 = √3/2
practice.why: Learners mix up which side goes on top, or use the wrong scale factor instead of the ratio.
practice.rightWay: Use the ratio from the drawing: wall/ladder = √3/2. Because the angle is the same, h/6 = √3/2, so h = 3√3 m.

lessons.title: Naming sides and using sin, cos and tan
objectives: You will be able to label the hypotenuse, opposite and adjacent sides with respect to a chosen angle.
You will be able to write sin theta, cos theta and tan theta as ratios of two sides.
You will be able to use SOH CAH TOA to choose the correct ratio.

keyWords.meaning: The side of a right-angled triangle opposite the right angle, and the longest side.
The side of the triangle that is across from the angle you are working with and does not touch it.
The side that touches the angle you are working with and is not the hypotenuse.
A fixed ratio of two sides of a right-angled triangle, fixed by the size of the angle.
Written sin, the ratio of the side opposite the angle to the hypotenuse.
Written cos, the ratio of the side adjacent to the angle to the hypotenuse.
Written tan, the ratio of the side opposite the angle to the side adjacent to the angle.
A memory aid that pairs each ratio with the two sides it uses.

blocks.text:
Last lesson you saw that similar right-angled triangles keep the same ratio between two sides. That is the idea behind trigonometry: once the angles of a right-angled triangle are fixed, the ratio of any two of its sides is fixed as well.

Trigonometry gives those fixed ratios names: sine, cosine and tangent. With a name you can write the ratio as a formula, and a formula lets you work out sides and angles you cannot measure directly.
blocks.speech: Last lesson you saw that similar right angled triangles keep the same ratio between two sides. That is the idea behind trigonometry. Once the angles of a right angled triangle are fixed, the ratio of any two of its sides is fixed as well. Trigonometry gives those fixed ratios names. They are called sine, cosine and tangent. With a name you can write the ratio as a formula, and a formula lets you work out sides and angles you cannot measure directly.

blocks.text: A right-angled triangle has three sides. The hypotenuse is the side opposite the right angle, and it is always the longest side. The other two sides are named according to the angle you are working with. The opposite side is the side across from that angle and it does not touch the angle. The adjacent side is the side that touches the angle but is not the hypotenuse.
blocks.speech: A right angled triangle has three sides. The hypotenuse is the side opposite the right angle, and it is always the longest side. The other two sides are named according to the angle you are working with. The opposite side is the side across from that angle, and it does not touch the angle. The adjacent side is the side that touches the angle but is not the hypotenuse.

blocks.caption: The right angle is at C. The angle θ is at A, so BC is the opposite side, AC is the adjacent side and AB is the hypotenuse.
blocks.speech: A right angled triangle A B C with the right angle at C. The angle theta is marked at A. The side across from the right angle, A B, is labelled hypotenuse. The side across from theta, B C, is labelled opposite. The side that touches theta and is not the hypotenuse, A C, is labelled adjacent.

blocks.text: The hypotenuse never changes, because the right angle never moves. But opposite and adjacent belong to the angle you choose. If you move to the other acute angle, the opposite and adjacent sides swap. The hypotenuse stays the same side: it is always the side opposite the right angle, and it is always the longest side.
blocks.speech: The hypotenuse never changes, because the right angle never moves. But opposite and adjacent belong to the angle you choose. If you move to the other acute angle, the opposite and adjacent sides swap. The hypotenuse stays the same side. It is always the side opposite the right angle, and it is always the longest side.

blocks.caption: The same triangle, but now the angle is α at B. The labels opposite and adjacent have swapped; the hypotenuse is still AB.
blocks.speech: The same triangle, but now the angle alpha is at B. The side across from alpha is A C, so A C is now the opposite side. The side that touches alpha and is not the hypotenuse is B C, so B C is now the adjacent side. The hypotenuse is still A B, the side opposite the right angle.

blocks.text:
For the angle θ:

sin θ = opposite/hypotenuse
cos θ = adjacent/hypotenuse
tan θ = opposite/adjacent

Remember SOH CAH TOA: S-O-H, sine is opposite over hypotenuse; C-A-H, cosine is adjacent over hypotenuse; T-O-A, tangent is opposite over adjacent. A ratio is a number, so it has no unit, and it does not change when the triangle is drawn bigger or smaller.
blocks.speech: For the angle theta, sine theta is the opposite side over the hypotenuse. Cosine theta is the adjacent side over the hypotenuse. Tangent theta is the opposite side over the adjacent side. Remember SOH CAH TOA. S O H means sine is opposite over hypotenuse. C A H means cosine is adjacent over hypotenuse. T O A means tangent is opposite over adjacent. A ratio is a number, so it has no unit, and it does not change when the triangle is drawn bigger or smaller.

blocks.problem: In triangle ABC, angle C = 90°, AB = 5, BC = 3 and AC = 4. Write down sin θ, where θ is the angle at A.

steps.reason: The hypotenuse is the side opposite the right angle at C.
θ is at A, and BC is the side across from A that does not touch it.
SOH tells us sine is opposite over hypotenuse.
Put the opposite side 3 over the hypotenuse 5.

blocks.speech: In triangle A B C, angle C is ninety degrees, A B is five, B C is three and A C is four. Write down sine theta, where theta is the angle at A. First, the hypotenuse is A B, which is five, because it is opposite the right angle at C. Second, the side opposite theta is B C, which is three, because theta is at A and B C is the side across from A. Third, SOH tells us sine is opposite over hypotenuse. So sine theta is three over five.

blocks.problem: In the same triangle, the angle at B is called α. Write down tan α.

steps.reason: α is at B, and AC is the side across from B that does not touch it.
BC touches B and is not the hypotenuse.
TOA tells us tangent is opposite over adjacent.
Put the opposite side 4 over the adjacent side 3.

blocks.speech: In the same triangle, the angle at B is called alpha. Write down tangent alpha. First, the side opposite alpha is A C, which is four, because alpha is at B and A C is across from B. Second, the side adjacent to alpha is B C, which is three, because it touches B and is not the hypotenuse. Third, TOA tells us tangent is opposite over adjacent. So tangent alpha is four over three.

question.prompt: In triangle ABC, angle C = 90°, AB = 13, BC = 5 and AC = 12. Write down cos A, where A is the angle at vertex A.
question.why: Learners often take the side opposite A, which is BC = 5, and write 5/13, which is sin A.
question.rightWay: The angle is at A, so the adjacent side is AC = 12 and the hypotenuse is AB = 13, giving cos A = 12/13.

blocks.hint: Which side touches A and is not the hypotenuse?
blocks.speech: In triangle A B C, angle C is ninety degrees, A B is thirteen, B C is five and A C is twelve. Write down cosine A, where A is the angle at vertex A. Pause here and try it yourself. The hypotenuse is A B, thirteen. The side adjacent to A is A C, twelve. So cosine A is twelve over thirteen.

blocks.problem: In triangle PQR, angle Q = 90°, PR = 10, PQ = 6 and QR = 8. Write down tan θ in simplest form, where θ is the angle at P.

steps.reason: The hypotenuse is the side opposite the right angle at Q.
θ is at P, and QR is the side across from P.
PQ touches P and is not the hypotenuse.
TOA: opposite over adjacent.
Divide the top and the bottom by 2 to simplify the fraction.

blocks.speech: In triangle P Q R, angle Q is ninety degrees, P R is ten, P Q is six and Q R is eight. Write down tangent theta in simplest form, where theta is the angle at P. First, the hypotenuse is P R, ten, because it is opposite the right angle at Q. Second, the side opposite theta is Q R, eight. Third, the side adjacent to theta is P Q, six. Fourth, tangent is opposite over adjacent, so we get eight over six. Divide top and bottom by two, and tangent theta is four over three.

blocks.problem: In triangle KLM, angle M = 90°, KL = 17, LM = 8 and KM = 15. Write down tan K, where K is the angle at vertex K.

steps.reason: The hypotenuse is the side opposite the right angle at M.
K is at vertex K, and LM is the side across from K.
KM touches K and is not the hypotenuse.
TOA: opposite over adjacent.

blocks.speech: In triangle K L M, angle M is ninety degrees, K L is seventeen, L M is eight and K M is fifteen. Write down tangent K, where K is the angle at vertex K. The hypotenuse is K L, seventeen, opposite the right angle at M. The side opposite K is L M, eight. The side adjacent to K is K M, fifteen. Tangent is opposite over adjacent, so tangent K is eight over fifteen.

blocks.why: The side of length 4 touches the angle θ, so it is the adjacent side and belongs to cosine. The side of length 3 is across from θ, so it is the opposite side. Sine is opposite over hypotenuse, which gives 3/5.
blocks.speech: Here is the usual mistake. In a triangle with theta at A, the side opposite theta is three, the side adjacent to theta is four and the hypotenuse is five. The wrong answer is sine theta equals four over five. The right answer is sine theta equals three over five. The side of length four touches the angle theta, so it is the adjacent side and belongs to cosine. The side of length three is across from theta, so it is the opposite side. Sine is opposite over hypotenuse, which gives three over five.

blocks.text: Before you write a ratio, do two things. First mark the angle you are working with. Then name the two sides the question talks about. The pair of names chooses the ratio. Opposite and hypotenuse: sine. Adjacent and hypotenuse: cosine. Opposite and adjacent: tangent. If the question links the side opposite the angle with the hypotenuse, you need sine.
blocks.speech: Before you write a ratio, do two things. First mark the angle you are working with. Then name the two sides the question talks about. The pair of names chooses the ratio. Opposite and hypotenuse gives sine. Adjacent and hypotenuse gives cosine. Opposite and adjacent gives tangent. If the question links the side opposite the angle with the hypotenuse, you need sine.

question.prompt: In triangle PQR, angle Q = 90°, PQ = 7, QR = 24 and PR = 25. Which statement is correct?
steps: Angle Q = 90°, so PR = 25 is the hypotenuse
For the angle at P the opposite side is QR = 24 and the adjacent side is PQ = 7
question.why: Learners who take PQ as the opposite side get sin P = 7/25, which is wrong.
question.rightWay: The angle is at P, so the opposite side is QR = 24 and the hypotenuse is PR = 25, giving sin P = 24/25.

blocks.hint: Mark the angle at P first, then decide which side is across from it.
blocks.speech: In triangle P Q R, angle Q is ninety degrees, P Q is seven, Q R is twenty four and P R is twenty five. Which statement is correct? The options are: A, sine P equals twenty four over twenty five. B, cosine P equals twenty four over twenty five. C, tangent P equals seven over twenty five. D, sine P equals seven over twenty four. Pause and try it. The right angle is at Q, so P R, twenty five, is the hypotenuse. For the angle at P the side across from it is Q R, twenty four, and the side touching it is P Q, seven. So sine P is twenty four over twenty five, which is option A.

blocks.text: To tie it together: the three ratios are only allowed in a right-angled triangle, so check for the right angle first. Then find the hypotenuse, name the other two sides according to the angle in the question, and let SOH CAH TOA pick the ratio. The answer is always a number: the ratio of two sides, with no unit.
blocks.speech: To tie it together. The three ratios are only allowed in a right angled triangle, so check for the right angle first. Then find the hypotenuse, name the other two sides according to the angle in the question, and let SOH CAH TOA pick the ratio. The answer is always a number. It is the ratio of two sides, and it has no unit.

summary: The hypotenuse is the side opposite the right angle and it is always the longest side.
The opposite and adjacent sides are named for the angle you use, so they swap when the angle changes.
sin θ = opposite/hypotenuse, cos θ = adjacent/hypotenuse, tan θ = opposite/adjacent.
SOH CAH TOA pairs each ratio with the two sides it needs.
These ratios only work in a right-angled triangle.

practice.prompt: In a right-angled triangle the angle θ is marked. The side opposite θ is 3, the side adjacent to θ is 4 and the hypotenuse is 5. Write down sin θ.
practice.why: Writing the adjacent side over the hypotenuse gives cos θ, not sin θ.
practice.rightWay: sin θ = opposite/hypotenuse = 3/5.

practice.prompt: In triangle ABC, angle C = 90°, AB = 13, AC = 12 and BC = 5. Write down cos A.
practice.why: The side opposite A is BC = 5, so using 5 gives sin A instead of cos A.
practice.rightWay: cos A = adjacent/hypotenuse = AC/AB = 12/13.

practice.prompt: In triangle DEF, angle F = 90°, DE = 26, EF = 10 and DF = 24. Write down tan D in simplest form.
practice.why: Using DE, the hypotenuse, in place of the adjacent side gives sin D instead of tan D.
practice.rightWay: tan D = opposite/adjacent = EF/DF = 10/24 = 5/12.

practice.prompt: In triangle XYZ, angle Z = 90°. Which statement is correct?
steps: Angle Z = 90°, so XY is the hypotenuse
For the angle at X the opposite side is YZ and the adjacent side is XZ
practice.why: Cosine uses the hypotenuse, so cos X = XZ/XY, not XZ/YZ.
practice.rightWay: sin X = YZ/XY, cos X = XZ/XY and tan X = YZ/XZ, so only A is correct.

practice.prompt: In a right-angled triangle the angle α is marked, the side opposite α is 15, the side adjacent to α is 20 and the hypotenuse is 25. Write down tan α in simplest form.
practice.why: Dividing the opposite side by the hypotenuse gives sin α, which is 3/5, not tan α.
practice.rightWay: tan α = opposite/adjacent = 15/20 = 3/4.

practice.prompt: Which statement is NOT correct?
steps: The statement tan θ = adjacent/opposite is not correct, so the answer is C
practice.why: Writing the adjacent side over the opposite side turns the tangent upside down.
practice.rightWay: TOA gives tan θ = opposite/adjacent, so option C is the one that is not correct.

practice.prompt: In triangle KLM, angle M = 90°, KL = 41, LM = 9 and KM = 40. Write down sin K + cos K.
practice.why: The two ratios must be written with the same hypotenuse KL = 41 before they can be added.
practice.rightWay: sin K = 9/41 and cos K = 40/41, so the sum is 49/41.

practice.prompt: In triangle PQR, angle Q = 90° and tan P = 5/12. The side opposite P is 10. Write down the length of the side adjacent to P.
practice.why: Multiplying the opposite side by 12/5 instead of 12/5 of it in the wrong order gives the wrong side.
practice.rightWay: The opposite side is 2 times the 5 in the ratio, so the adjacent side is 2 times 12, which is 24.

lessons.title: Reciprocal ratios on the calculator
objectives: You will be able to write cosec, sec and cot as reciprocals of sin, cos and tan.
You will be able to find sin, cos and tan values on a calculator in degree mode.
You will be able to calculate reciprocal ratios by using 1 over sin, cos or tan.

keyWords.meaning: The reciprocal of a number is 1 divided by that number, for example the reciprocal of 2 is 1/2.
Cosecant, written cosec or csc, is the reciprocal of sin: cosec θ = 1/sin θ.
Secant, written sec, is the reciprocal of cos: sec θ = 1/cos θ.
Cotangent, written cot, is the reciprocal of tan: cot θ = 1/tan θ.
The calculator setting where angles are measured in degrees, which you must check before any trigonometry.
The longest side of a right-angled triangle, always opposite the right angle.
The side of a right-angled triangle that does not touch the angle you are working with.
The side of a right-angled triangle that touches the angle you are working with and is not the hypotenuse.

blocks.text:
In the last lesson you met the three main ratios: sin, cos and tan. Each of them has a partner called a reciprocal ratio. A reciprocal simply means 1 divided by the ratio.

The three reciprocal ratios are cosecant (cosec), secant (sec) and cotangent (cot):

cosec θ = 1/sin θ
sec θ = 1/cos θ
cot θ = 1/tan θ

Why do we need them? Some exam questions and some real problems are easier to write using cosec, sec or cot, so you must be able to convert them back to sin, cos and tan to work with them.
blocks.speech: In the last lesson you met sin, cos and tan. Each one has a partner called a reciprocal ratio. A reciprocal means one divided by the ratio. Cosec theta is one over sin theta. Sec theta is one over cos theta. Cot theta is one over tan theta. Why do we need them? Some exam questions use these names, so you must be able to turn them back into sin, cos and tan to work with them.

blocks.text:
There is no cosec, sec or cot button on your calculator. That is the whole point of this lesson: you convert the reciprocal ratio to sin, cos or tan first, then use 1 divided by that value.

For example, to find sec 34° you press 1 ÷ ( cos 34° ). The calculator gives 1,2062..., which is 1,21 correct to two decimal places.

Before you start any calculator work, check that your calculator is in degrees mode. A small D or Deg on the screen tells you it is set correctly.

For example, to find sec thirty four degrees, press one divided by cos thirty four degrees. The calculator gives about one point two one. Before you start, check that your calculator is in degrees mode.

blocks.caption: A right-angled triangle showing the hypotenuse, the adjacent side and the opposite side for angle θ.
blocks.speech: This picture shows a right-angled triangle. The angle theta is at one corner. The side opposite the right angle is the hypotenuse. The side next to theta is the adjacent side. The side across from theta is the opposite side. The reciprocal ratios use these same sides, just upside down: cosec theta is hypotenuse over opposite, sec theta is hypotenuse over adjacent, and cot theta is adjacent over opposite.

blocks.text:
In a right-angled triangle the reciprocal ratios have side meanings too, the flip of the main ratios:

cosec θ = hypotenuse/opposite
sec θ = hypotenuse/adjacent
cot θ = adjacent/opposite

Notice that sin θ × cosec θ = 1, cos θ × sec θ = 1 and tan θ × cot θ = 1. A ratio times its reciprocal always gives 1, just like 2 × 1/2 = 1.
blocks.speech: In a right-angled triangle the reciprocal ratios use the sides flipped over. Cosec theta is hypotenuse over opposite. Sec theta is hypotenuse over adjacent. Cot theta is adjacent over opposite. Also notice that a ratio times its reciprocal always gives one, just like two times one half gives one.

blocks.problem: Use your calculator to find sec 34°, correct to two decimal places.

steps.reason: There is no sec button, so write sec as 1 over cos.
Press 1 ÷ ( cos 34° ) in degrees mode and find cos 34°.
Divide 1 by the cosine value.
Round to two decimal places.

blocks.speech: Find sec thirty four degrees correct to two decimal places. There is no sec button, so write sec thirty four degrees as one over cos thirty four degrees. Press one divided by, open bracket, cos, thirty four, close bracket. The calculator gives one point two zero six two, which rounds to one point two one.

blocks.problem: Use your calculator to find cot 49°, correct to two decimal places.

steps.reason: Write cot as 1 over tan, since there is no cot button.
Press 1 ÷ ( tan 49° ) in degrees mode.
Divide 1 by the tangent value.
Round to two decimal places.

blocks.speech: Find cot forty nine degrees correct to two decimal places. Write cot forty nine degrees as one over tan forty nine degrees. Press one divided by, open bracket, tan, forty nine, close bracket. The calculator gives zero point eight six nine three, which rounds to zero point eight seven.

blocks.problem: A right-angled triangle has an angle θ. The side opposite θ is 3 and the hypotenuse is 5. Find cosec θ without a calculator, then check your answer with the calculator.

steps.reason: Cosec is the flip of sin, so it is hypotenuse over opposite.
Substitute the hypotenuse 5 and the opposite side 3.
Divide 5 by 3 to get the value as a decimal.
Cosec is 1 over sin, so the two answers must match.

blocks.speech: A right-angled triangle has an angle theta. The side opposite theta is three and the hypotenuse is five. Find cosec theta without a calculator, then check with the calculator. Cosec theta is hypotenuse over opposite, so five over three, which is about one point six seven. To check: sin theta is three over five, which is zero point six, and one over zero point six is also about one point six seven. The two answers match.

question.prompt: Use your calculator to find cosec 25°, correct to two decimal places.
question.why: Learners often press sin 25° and give 0,42, forgetting to take the reciprocal 1 over the value.
question.rightWay: Write cosec 25° as 1/sin 25° first, then divide 1 by sin 25° on the calculator in degrees mode. The answer is 2,37.

blocks.hint: Cosec is 1 over sin, so find sin 25° first and then divide 1 by it.
blocks.speech: Your turn. Use your calculator to find cosec twenty five degrees, correct to two decimal places. Hint: cosec is one over sin, so find sin twenty five degrees first and then divide one by it.

blocks.why: Sec is not the same as cos. Sec is the reciprocal, 1 divided by cos. Leaving out the 1 over gives a completely different number.
blocks.speech: A common mistake: writing sec thirty four degrees as just cos thirty four degrees, which gives zero point eight three. The right way is sec thirty four degrees equals one over cos thirty four degrees, which gives one point two one. The mistake happens because sec is the reciprocal of cos, so the one over part cannot be left out.

blocks.text:
Putting it together: every reciprocal ratio starts the same way. Replace the name with 1 over the main ratio, then use the calculator.

sec θ = 1/cos θ, cosec θ = 1/sin θ, cot θ = 1/tan θ.

In a triangle the sides flip: cosec is hypotenuse/opposite, sec is hypotenuse/adjacent, cot is adjacent/opposite. Check your calculator is in degrees mode, round to two decimal places, and you are ready for exam questions like sec 34° or cot 49°.
blocks.speech: To put it together: every reciprocal ratio starts the same way. Replace the name with one over the main ratio, then use the calculator. Sec theta is one over cos theta, cosec theta is one over sin theta, and cot theta is one over tan theta. In a triangle the sides flip over. Check your calculator is in degrees mode and round to two decimal places.

summary: cosec θ = 1/sin θ, sec θ = 1/cos θ, cot θ = 1/tan θ.
In a triangle: cosec θ = hypotenuse/opposite, sec θ = hypotenuse/adjacent, cot θ = adjacent/opposite.
A ratio times its reciprocal gives 1: sin θ × cosec θ = 1, and so on.
